report.summary: Outbox publication throttled to about 16 per 10 s against 26 arrivals, so the backlog grew. The consumer handler adds about 510 ms to a share of deliveries. LedgerCore's DB, pool and transfers endpoint look healthy.

findings.claim: The outbox backlog grew while arrivals stayed steady: publications dropped from 26 to about 13-17 per 10 s, then caught up with 79-81 per 10 s at the end.
findings.reason: Arrivals are flat at 26 per 10 s; pending rose from 2 to 115 and the oldest undelivered age reached 44 s, with no failures.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts succeed but a share are slow (p95 584 ms vs p50 72 ms). The extra time is in the consumer handler (p95 510 ms), not auth or LedgerCore overhead.
findings.reason: Consumer handler p95 is 510 ms while auth stays about 70 ms and unattributed time is about 1 ms; all 384 attempts are SUCCESS.

findings.claim: The slow consumer handler plausibly caps the serial outbox poller's throughput below the arrival rate, which would explain the late notifications.
findings.reason: If a batch of 20 is delivered one at a time, the 510 ms handler stalls cut throughput to about 16 per 10 s, below 26 per 10 s. Delivery order was not observed.

limitations: Only the first 100 of 384 attempt rows are listed, and the log shows 384 attempt records against 393 attempts reported by poll batches (a 9-attempt gap).
The consumer is a test fixture, so its 510 ms handler delay may not reflect production, and why it is slow is not shown.
next_checks: Check why the consumer handler takes about 510 ms for part of the traffic, and whether the delays cluster in the 15:57-15:58 window.
Confirm whether the poller delivers a batch serially, and reconcile the 393 vs 384 attempt count gap.

report.summary: Outbox publications fell to about 60% of arrivals, so a backlog built and notifications aged up to 44 s. Slow consumer handler time (~510 ms) is the likely cause. The cause of that slowness is not shown.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog grew while arrivals were steady: pending rose from 2 to a peak of 115 and the oldest undelivered age reached 44 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals held at 26 per 10 s, but publications dropped to 13-17 per 10 s, then spiked to 79-81 at the end as the backlog drained.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts slowed because the consumer handler took up to ~510 ms, so total delivery time rose from ~72 ms (p50) to ~580 ms (p95).
findings.reason: Consumer auth stayed at about 70 ms and unattributed time was about 1 ms. Handler time p95 was 510 ms. Delivery logs show about 578 ms successes later in the window.

findings.claim: The slower, probably serialized delivery attempts cut publisher throughput below the arrival rate, which created the delay. Failures, retries, the database and the pool did not contribute.
findings.reason: All 384 attempts succeeded, with no failures or errors. The pool had no waits and no blocking sessions were sampled. The ~16 per 10 s publication rate is roughly consistent with ~0.6 s per sequential delivery.

limitations: The handler is a test fixture consumer, so its slowness may not reflect a real consumer. The evidence does not show why the handler became slow or when exactly it started.
The delivery log listing covers only the earliest 100 of 384 records, and 393 attempts reported by poll batches versus 384 records is a small unexplained gap.
